transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom / recorded
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Rosa Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Head of ML, Aquila), Liam O'Connor (VP Eng), Samir Bose (SRE), Elena Park (PM)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Aquila is preparing for a Q3 rollout of generative product features; main objectives are lowering per-token cost, hitting 95th percentile latency SLOs under 200ms for interactive flows, and confirming a path to Dedicated/VPC if audit/residency needs tighten. Redwood outlined batching, KV caching, and Dedicated capacity options. Action items include benchmark plan, request histogram share, and pilot pricing proposal.

Topics:
- Current usage and cost profile
- Latency SLOs and tail latencies
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
- Benchmark plan and sample datasets
- Security/compliance and audit log cadence
- Rollout runway and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, we'll do a quick readout and then jump to the perf stuff. is that okay?
[00:07] Priya Nair: yep sounds good, thanks Maya. quick context: Q3 GA for our agent features, expecting about 25k daily active users at launch, and bursts up to 3x during promos.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: timeline's tight, we're trying to get a cost target under control — current per-conversation cost is about $0.75 and we need to get closer to $0.20 for viability.
[00:28] Jonah Patel: ok good, so two parallel things — first we can help with batching, quantization profiles and prefix KV caching to reduce token compute; second is capacity mode, Dedicated helps stabilize tail latency and gives predictable unit price.
[00:40] Samir Bose: quick Q, when you say KV cache can we pre-warm cache across replicas? we saw cold-start token spikes last month.
[00:48] Jonah Patel: yeah so we have prefix caching and shard-local KV strategies, but there are tradeoffs: pre-warm helps tail but increases memory. and sometimes the transcriber of the call will show it as K-V cash (laugh), but it's the same idea.
[00:59] Priya: and how much does quantization impact quality? we tried int8 and got weird hallucination shifts on system prompts.
[01:06] Jonah: good question; in our experience int8 works well for short-context ranking and embeddings, for long-system prompt tasks we recommend mixed precision or model-specific quant profiles. we can run a quality regression (evals) against your prompt set — that's part of the benchmark plan.
[01:22] Maya: to set expectations, Dedicated will give you lower tail latency and a committed, lower unit cost if you sign a monthly reserve. Hosted is fastest to start but variable cost and possibly higher tails during bursts. Private/VPC gets you the network and audit controls but adds ops overhead.
[01:36] Elena Park: regarding compliance: Priya's team needs audit logs and an exportable trail for SOC2 internal audit; SSO + SAML and KMS integration too.
[01:44] Rosa Alvarez: we have a SOC 2 Pack and KMS integration doc, we'll share the security bundle. Redwood supports bring-your-own-key via KMS and we keep detailed per-request logs with retention options.
[01:56] Liam: latency SLOs — we love the idea of automated fallback to smaller model variants during congestion. is that something you can configure at route level?
[02:03] Jonah: yes, smart routing policies can be set per-route. e.g., low-latency route -> prefer 8-bit quantized variant with prefix cache, fallback to hosted smaller model if Dedicated is saturated. we'll show routing examples in the perf plan.
[02:16] Priya: can you also show the real unit economics — like tokens per call and effective cost after caching? our CFO will want that in the pilot proposal.
[02:25] Maya: absolutely we'll include a token-level cost breakdown with sample savings from batching and caching.
[02:31] [02:30] Samir: quick note — our infra team uses GKE in us-west1 and we prefer VPC peering for Private. if we go Private how heavy is the on-prem package? we might be air-gapped in some regions.
[02:42] Jonah: the Private control plane supports VPC peering and optional on-prem runtime; air-gapped installs require an ops window and additional deployment checklist. we'll put the deployment matrix in the handoff doc.
[02:52] Priya: okay for the benchmark, we can share a 7-day window of request histograms and top 20 user prompts. we want the benchmark to simulate 90th and 95th percentile likely customers.
[03:03] Maya: perfect. next up we'll propose two pilot tracks: 1) Hosted pilot with caching + batching optimizations for 4 weeks, and 2) Dedicated reserved pilot with autoscale and canary rollout for production readiness. both include evals against your prompt set.
[03:16] Liam: what are the signal gates to move from Hosted pilot to Dedicated?
[03:19] Rosa: usually it's predictable load above X RPS or tail latency failures, plus org-level commit to cost. We'll propose thresholds in the SLO playbook.
[03:28] [03:30] Jonah: also want to call out model deprecation concerns — if you pin a model version in Dedicated we support rollouts and canarying to avoid regressions. automatic fallback to compatible variants is a safety net.
[03:40] Priya: we’ve had a concern around hallucinations increasing after quantization — please include the evaluation metrics (BLEU-ish similarity, hallucination count, problematic answer audit) in the quality report.
[03:50] Jonah: we'll run the redwood evals suite and include a hallucination regression metric and per-prompt diffs.
[03:55] Maya: ok before we wrap, let's recap action items. Samir will share the histograms and prompts, Jonah will prepare perf plan and benchmarking steps, Maya will send pilot pricing and committed capacity options, Rosa will share security artifacts and onboarding channel.
[04:09] Priya: sounds good. can we do a 30 minute perf run next Tuesday? Samir and Jonah will be on that call.
[04:15] Maya: yes we'll send a calendar invite for 30 minutes; Jonah, can you take the lead?
[04:19] Jonah: yep I'll schedule and add the perf checklist.
[04:22] Elena: also please include a short doc on rollback procedures in case of a model regression after rollout.
[04:27] Jonah: will do — we'll include canary thresholds and rollback steps.
[04:31] [04:30] Liam: last Q — competitors, Anthropic was mentioned earlier; our procurement team asked if there were any feature gaps vs Vertex style managed endpoints.
[04:40] Maya: the main differences are in observability and rollout controls; Redwood emphasizes per-token cost breakdowns and SLO routing with built-in fallbacks. we'll include a short competitor feature comparison note.
[04:52] Priya: great. thanks everyone, excited to see the perf plan.
[04:56] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the pilot pricing and schedule.

End of transcript.
